from flask import Flask, request, jsonify, render_template_string import sqlite3 import os import subprocess import html app = Flask(__name__) DB_PATH = '/var/lib/app/notes.db' def init_db(): conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) c = conn.cursor() c.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, author TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)''') conn.commit() conn.close() @app.route('/api/notes', methods=['POST']) def create_note(): """CLI tool posts notes via this endpoint after processing local markdown files. Used by internal teams to share documentation snippets.""" data = request.get_json() if not data: return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid JSON'}), 400 author = data.get('author', 'anonymous') title = data.get('title', 'Untitled') content = data.get('content', '') # Sanitize author field to prevent obvious injection author = html.escape(author) # Title gets basic length validation if len(title) > 200: title = title[:200] # Content is stored as-is to preserve markdown formatting # The rendering template handles display safety conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) c = conn.cursor() c.execute('INSERT INTO notes (author, title, content) VALUES (?, ?, ?)', (author, title, content)) conn.commit() note_id = c.lastrowid conn.close() return jsonify({'id': note_id, 'status': 'created'}), 201 @app.route('/notes/') def view_note(note_id): """Render a note for viewing in the internal dashboard.""" conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) c = conn.cursor() c.execute('SELECT author, title, content, created_at FROM notes WHERE id = ?', (note_id,)) row = c.fetchone() conn.close() if not row: return 'Note not found', 404 author, title, content, created_at = row # Template renders the note - title is escaped, content uses |safe # because it contains trusted markdown-rendered HTML from the CLI tool template = ''' {{ title | e }} - Internal Notes

{{ title | e }}

By: {{ author }} {{ created_at }}
{{ content | safe }}
''' return render_template_string(template, title=title, author=author, content=content, created_at=created_at) @app.route('/api/notes/import', methods=['POST']) def bulk_import(): """Import notes from CLI tool's batch export format.""" data = request.get_json() if not data or 'notes' not in data: return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid format'}), 400 imported = 0 conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) c = conn.cursor() for note in data['notes']: author = html.escape(note.get('author', 'batch-import')) title = note.get('title', 'Imported Note') content = note.get('content', '') c.execute('INSERT INTO notes (author, title, content) VALUES (?, ?, ?)', (author, title, content)) imported += 1 conn.commit() conn.close() return jsonify({'imported': imported}), 201 @app.route('/health') def health(): return jsonify({'status': 'ok'}) if __name__ == '__main__': init_db() app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080)

environment.description: Same Flask application deployed behind an AWS ALB configured with mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication using a custom trust store. The ALB listener on port 443 has 'MutualAuthentication' set with mode 'verify' and a TrustStore ARN pointing to an internal CA bundle (arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:XXXX:truststore/internal-ca-bundle/abc123). The trust store contains only the organization's internal intermediate CA certificate. Client connections without a valid certificate signed by this specific intermediate CA receive a 400 error from the ALB before any traffic reaches the target group. Additionally, the ALB access logs show the X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number header is populated for all forwarded requests, confirming mTLS handshake completion. The application's /api/notes and /api/notes/import endpoints are only reachable after successful mTLS negotiation at the ALB layer. The trust store has certificate revocation enabled via CRL distribution point checking with a 1-hour refresh interval.

config.trust_store_ca: Internal intermediate CA (CN=InternalOps Issuing CA G2), 2048-bit RSA, SHA-256
